questions.question: What is the navigation path to create a new Event Field Mapping in ServiceNow?

options.text: All > Event Management > Configuration > Field Mapping
All > Event Management > Rules > Event Field Mapping
All > System Definition > Event Mapping
All > ITOM > Event Configuration > Mappings

explanation.correct: Event Field Mappings are accessed via All > Event Management > Rules > Event Field Mapping. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/t_EMCreateEventFieldMapping2.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Incorrect navigation path
System Definition is for platform configuration, not Event Management
This navigation path does not exist

source.excerpt: Navigate to All > Event Management > Rules > Event Field Mapping.

questions.question: Which three mapping types are available when creating an Event Field Mapping? (Choose three.)

options.text: Map field and transform value (Single field)
Map field (Copy field)
Map field using database query
Advanced mapping using script
Map field using LDAP lookup

explanation.correct: Event Field Mapping supports several mapping types including: Map field and transform value (Single field), Map field (Copy field), and Advanced mapping using script. Other types include Map field and transform value using regex and Map field from reference table. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/t_EMCreateEventFieldMapping2.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Database query is not a direct mapping type; use reference table instead
LDAP lookup is not an Event Field Mapping type

source.excerpt: Mapping type options include: Map field and transform value (Single field), Map field (Copy field), Advanced mapping using script, Map field and transform value using regex, Map field from reference table.

questions.question: Which role is required to create and configure Event Field Mappings?

options.text: itil
evt_mgmt_admin
admin
evt_mgmt_user

explanation.correct: The evt_mgmt_admin role is required to create and configure Event Field Mappings. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/t_EMCreateEventFieldMapping2.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: itil role is for ITSM tasks, not Event Management configuration
Admin has access but evt_mgmt_admin is the specific required role
evt_mgmt_user is a different role with fewer permissions

questions.question: In the event processing workflow, what happens when an event rule has the 'Ignore' checkbox selected?

options.text: The event is deleted from the system
No alert is generated, but the event is still available for review
The event is forwarded to another instance
An incident is created instead of an alert

explanation.correct: If the rule Ignore checkbox is selected, no alert is generated. However, the event is still available for review and remediation. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/em-process-flow.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Events are retained even when ignored
Ignore does not forward events
Ignore prevents alert generation, not incident creation

source.excerpt: Ignore Rule: If the rule Ignore check box is selected, no alert is generated. However, the event is still available for review and remediation.

questions.question: When multiple event rules are defined for the same type of event, how does Event Management determine which rule to apply first?

options.text: Alphabetically by rule name
By the rule order field
By creation date (oldest first)
Randomly selected

explanation.correct: If multiple rules are defined for the same type of event, use the rule order to determine the sequence of rule application. Rules with lower order numbers are processed first. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/em-process-flow.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Rule order field determines sequence, not alphabetical name
Creation date does not determine rule execution order
Rule execution follows a defined order, not random

source.excerpt: If multiple rules are defined for the same type of event, use the rule order to determine the sequence of rule application.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Threshold Accumulation setting in Event Management?

options.text: To limit the number of events stored in the database
To accumulate events until a threshold is met, then generate a single alert
To set a maximum severity level for alerts
To control memory usage on the MID Server

explanation.correct: If Active in the threshold section is selected, accumulate all events until the threshold is met, then generate a single alert for the events. This prevents alert storms from many similar events. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/em-process-flow.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Threshold accumulation is for alert generation, not database storage limits
Severity is set separately, not by thresholds
MID Server memory is managed separately

source.excerpt: Threshold Accumulation: If Active in the threshold section is selected, accumulate all events until the threshold is met, then generate a single alert for the events.

questions.question: How does Event Management determine if an alert already exists when processing an event?

options.text: By comparing the event description
By searching for a matching message key
By checking the source IP address
By comparing timestamps

explanation.correct: Event Management searches the Alert [em_alert] table for a matching message key. If a matching message key exists, it updates the alert; if not, it creates a new alert. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/em-process-flow.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Description is not used for alert matching
IP address alone doesn't determine alert matching
Timestamps are not used for matching existing alerts

source.excerpt: Alert Generation: Search the Alert [em_alert] table for a matching message key. If a matching message key exists, update the alert according to the event information.

questions.question: When configuring an Event Field Mapping with the 'Run after binding' option enabled, which two prefixes can be used to retrieve values from the CI record? (Choose two.)

options.text: alert_cmdb_ci.
ci_record.
alert_cmdb_ci_key.
cmdb_binding.

explanation.correct: When 'Run after binding' is enabled, use alert_cmdb_ci. to retrieve a field from the CI record (e.g., alert_cmdb_ci.assignment_group), and alert_cmdb_ci_key. to retrieve a value from the CMDB Tags table (e.g., alert_cmdb_ci_key.subscription). Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/t_EMCreateEventFieldMapping2.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: ci_record is not a valid prefix for Event Field Mapping
cmdb_binding is not a valid prefix

source.excerpt: Use alert_cmdb_ci. to retrieve a field from the CI record. Use alert_cmdb_ci_key. to retrieve a value from the CMDB Tags table.

questions.question: What is a potential impact of using complex scripts in 'Advanced mapping using script' Event Field Mappings?

options.text: Increased database storage requirements
Event processing performance degradation
MID Server connection failures
Alert notification delays only

explanation.correct: Complex scripts in Event Field Mappings may affect event processing performance. ServiceNow warns that complex scripts should be used carefully. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/t_EMCreateEventFieldMapping2.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Storage is not directly affected by script complexity
Script complexity doesn't cause MID Server connection issues
Performance impact affects all processing, not just notifications

source.excerpt: Warning: Complex scripts may affect event processing performance.

questions.question: In Team-based integrations for Event Field Mapping, what happens when no assignment group is defined in the rule?

options.text: The rule is disabled
The rule is considered global and runs before team-specific rules
The rule only runs for admin users
The rule is automatically assigned to the default group

explanation.correct: If no assignment group is defined in the event field-mapping rule, the rule is considered global. When rules run, global rules execute first, then rules belonging to the assignment group that the event's source instance belongs to. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/t_EMCreateEventFieldMapping2.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Unassigned rules are not disabled, they become global
Global rules run for all events, not just admin users
Rules without assignment groups become global, not assigned to default

source.excerpt: If no assignment group is defined in the event field-mapping rule, then this rule is considered global. When the rules are running – first the global rules run and then the rules that belong to the assignment group.

questions.question: Which prefix should be used to define alert tags in an Event Field Mapping Target field?

options.text: tag_
t_
alert_tag_
@tag:

explanation.correct: Alert tags can be defined in the Target field by using the <t_> prefix. For example, t_custom_tag would create or update an alert tag. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/t_EMCreateEventFieldMapping2.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: tag_ is not the correct prefix for alert tags
alert_tag_ is not the correct prefix
@tag: is not a valid ServiceNow prefix

source.excerpt: Alert tags can also be defined by using the <t_> prefix.

questions.question: What happens if an event has no severity after event transformations are applied?

options.text: The event is assigned a default severity of 'Info'
An alert is created with severity 'Unknown'
The event is retained for reference but no alert is generated
The event is discarded from the system

explanation.correct: If the event has no severity after the event transformations, retain the event for reference purposes and do not generate an alert. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/em-process-flow.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: No default severity is assigned; the event simply doesn't generate an alert
No alert is created when severity is missing
Events are retained for reference, never discarded

source.excerpt: If the event has no severity after the event transformations, retain the event for reference purposes and do not generate an alert.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Event Field Mapping are true?
a) Source field can include event fields and additional info fields
b) Target field can be an alert tag using the t_ prefix
c) Filter conditions can use Add Filter Condition and Add OR Clause
d) Event Field Mappings run synchronously on every event regardless of the filter

options.text: a, b, c, and d
a, b, and c only
a and b only
b and d only

explanation.correct: Statements a, b, and c are true. Statement d is false because Event Field Mappings only run when the filter conditions are met, not on every event regardless of filter. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/t_EMCreateEventFieldMapping2.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Statement d is false - mappings only run when filter matches
Statement c is also true - multiple filter conditions are supported
Statement a is also true about source fields

source.excerpt: Source field includes all event and additional info fields. Alert tags can be defined by using the t_ prefix. Select Add Filter Condition or Add OR Clause to configure multiple conditions.

questions.question: An administrator wants to populate the alert assignment_group field with the value from the CI's assignment group. Which mapping configuration should be used?

options.text: Source field: ci.assignment_group, Target field: assignment_group
Source field: alert_cmdb_ci.assignment_group, Target field: assignment_group, with Run after binding enabled
Source field: cmdb_ci.assignment_group, Target field: alert.assignment_group
Source field: CI_assignment_group, Target field: alert_assignment_group

explanation.correct: To retrieve values from the CI record, use the alert_cmdb_ci. prefix and enable 'Run after binding'. This allows the mapping to access CI fields after the alert has been bound to a CI. Example: alert_cmdb_ci.assignment_group populates the alert assignment_group field. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/t_EMCreateEventFieldMapping2.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: ci. is not the correct prefix for accessing CI fields in Event Field Mapping
cmdb_ci. is not the correct prefix; use alert_cmdb_ci. with Run after binding
These field names are not valid in Event Field Mapping

source.excerpt: Use 'alert_cmdb_ci.assignment_group' to populate (and transform) an alert 'assignment_group' field with the value of the CI's assignment group.

questions.question: What is the maximum character length for the Source field in an Event Field Mapping?

options.text: 50 characters
100 characters
200 characters
255 characters

explanation.correct: The Source field in Event Field Mapping has a maximum length of 100 characters. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/t_EMCreateEventFieldMapping2.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: 50 characters is too short; the limit is 100
200 characters exceeds the actual limit of 100
255 characters exceeds the actual limit of 100

source.excerpt: Source: Event monitoring software that generated the event. Maximum length: 100 characters.

questions.question: Which is NOT supported as a filter field for Alert Management Rules?

options.text: Severity
Source
Priority Group
Description

explanation.correct: Priority Group, along with Overall Event Count, Priority, Priority Breakdown, Tags, and Impacted Services are NOT supported for alert filtering in Alert Management Rules. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/alert-management-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Severity can be used for alert filtering
Source can be used for alert filtering
Description can be used for alert filtering

source.excerpt: The fields that are not supported for alert filtering are: Overall Event Count, Priority, Priority Group, Priority Breakdown, Tags, and Impacted Services.

questions.question: By default, what fields are concatenated to populate the Message Key if it is not provided in an event?

options.text: Source, Node, and Severity
Source, Type, Node, Resource, and Metric Name
Node, Resource, Description, and Severity
Source, CI, and Description

explanation.correct: If the Message Key is not populated, the system concatenates the Source, Type, Node, Resource, and Metric Name fields to populate the Message Key. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/c_EMEventIdentifier.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Severity is not part of the Message Key concatenation.
Description and Severity are not part of the default Message Key fields.
CI and Description are not part of the default Message Key concatenation.

questions.question: What is the effect of event rules on event records in the Event table?

options.text: Event rules directly modify the event records in the Event table
Event rules do not change event records; changes are stored in instance memory
Event rules delete processed events from the Event table
Event rules move events from the Event table to the Alert table

explanation.correct: Event rules do not change the event records in the Event table. Changes to event data are stored in the ServiceNow instance memory. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/create-event-rules.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Event rules never modify event records directly in the Event table.
Event rules do not delete events; events remain for review regardless of rule processing.
Event rules do not move events; they process events and generate alerts as separate records.

questions.question: An administrator wants to test how a specific event will be processed without affecting production alerts. What feature should they use?

options.text: Event forwarding
Simulate event processing
Event field mapping preview
Event rule dry run

explanation.correct: The Simulate event processing feature allows you to simulate event processing logic on events and display the resulting alert without creating actual alerts. Access it from an event record's Related Links section. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/simulate-event-processing.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Event forwarding sends events to external systems; it does not simulate processing.
There is no specific 'Event field mapping preview' feature.
The feature is called 'Simulate event processing', not 'Event rule dry run'.

questions.question: Where are event field mappings applied in the event processing flow?

options.text: Before event rule processing
After event rule processing and prior to alert generation
After alert generation
During event collection by the MID Server

explanation.correct: Event field mappings apply after event rule processing and prior to alert generation. The mapping values from the Event Mapping Pair table apply to the alert, while the original event severity remains unchanged. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/c_EMEventFieldMapping.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Event field mappings are applied after event rule processing, not before.
Mappings are applied prior to alert generation, not after.
Event field mappings are processed on the instance, not during MID Server collection.

questions.question: What happens to event field mapping rules when processing events that have no matching event rule?

options.text: Event field mappings are skipped entirely
The system still searches for and applies event field mappings
A default mapping is automatically created
The event is discarded without creating an alert

explanation.correct: In the event processing flow, the system searches for an event field mapping even if there was no matching event rule. If a mapping is found, it is applied. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/em-process-flow.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Event field mappings are always searched for, regardless of whether an event rule was matched.
No default mapping is automatically created; existing mappings are searched.
Events without matching rules are not discarded; they can still generate alerts through field mappings.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'Apply additional matching rules' check box in an event rule?

options.text: To apply the rule to events from multiple sources simultaneously
To run multiple sequential rules defined for the same event
To apply the rule to both events and alerts
To enable the rule to run on closed alerts

explanation.correct: Selecting 'Apply additional matching rules' allows multiple sequential rules defined for the same event to run in ascending order as defined in the Order field. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/create-event-rules.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This option controls sequential rule execution, not multi-source application.
Event rules process events only, not alerts directly.
Event rules process events, not closed alerts.

questions.question: How does Event Management handle table rotation for the em_event table by default?

options.text: Events are deleted after 24 hours
The em_event table is rotated to an offload table with base table cleanup after seven rotations
Events are archived to a cold storage table monthly
Table rotation is disabled by default and must be manually enabled

explanation.correct: By default, the table rotation for Event Management rotates the em_event table to an offload table and the base table cleanup takes place after seven table rotations. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/event-table-rotation.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Events are not simply deleted after 24 hours; table rotation manages data growth.
There is no cold storage archival; table rotation uses offload tables.
Table rotation is used by Event Management by default.

questions.question: An administrator receives events with a custom field 'org_severity' containing values Low, Medium, and High. How should they map these to standard alert severity values?

options.text: Create event rules with transform scripts for each severity level
Create an Event Field Mapping rule with Transform Value Pairs
Modify the event directly using a business rule on the em_event table
Configure a custom connector to translate severity values

explanation.correct: Event Field Mapping rules with Transform Value Pairs are designed for exactly this purpose - mapping values from specific event fields to alert field values. For example, mapping org_severity Low→Warning, Medium→Major, High→Critical. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/c_EMEventFieldMapping.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: While event rule transforms could work, Event Field Mappings with Transform Value Pairs is the purpose-built feature for this.
Modifying events directly via business rules is not the recommended approach; Event Field Mappings preserve the original event.
Connectors handle event collection, not severity value translation.

questions.question: What is the purpose of alert tags in Event Management?

options.text: To categorize alerts by business unit for reporting
To consolidate normalized fields and improve admin experience for transforming alert fields (key/value)
To assign priority scores to alerts
To create visual labels on the Event Management dashboard

explanation.correct: Alert tags consolidate all normalized fields and improve the admin experience to transform and normalize alert fields (key/value), enabling reuse of normalized fields across different sources. This improves alert quality for correlation and provides more out-of-the-box TBAC definitions. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/processing-events.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Alert tags are for field normalization and correlation, not business unit categorization.
Alert tags do not directly assign priority scores.
Alert tags are not visual dashboard labels; they are normalized key/value pairs.

questions.question: What does team-based integration in Event Management ensure regarding event rule execution?

options.text: Each team's rules run independently without any ordering
Connector ownership and execution of rules give precedence to global rules
Team rules always override global rules
Rules are executed alphabetically by team name

explanation.correct: Team-based integrations ensure that connector ownership and execution of rules give precedence to global rules. Event rules applied to assignment groups only run after the global rules have run. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/create-event-rules.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Team rules are ordered with respect to global rules; global rules run first.
Global rules take precedence and run before team-specific rules.
Rules are not executed alphabetically; they follow the global-first, team-second ordering.

questions.question: An administrator wants to view the rules that will be applied to a specific event before it is processed. Where can they find this information?

options.text: Navigate to Event Management > Rules > Event Rule Simulator
Open the event record and select 'Simulate event processing' from Related Links
Run the 'Event Rule Analysis' scheduled job
Check the Event Management dashboard analytics

explanation.correct: You can simulate event processing by opening an event from All Events, then selecting 'Simulate event processing' from the Related Links section. The Activities tab shows which rules and mappings were applied. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/simulate-event-processing.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: There is no separate 'Event Rule Simulator' navigation path; the simulation is accessed from individual event records.
There is no 'Event Rule Analysis' scheduled job; simulation is done per-event from the event record.
Dashboard analytics show trends, not per-event rule application details.
